New machine. Its objects are: nedupon, letesi, vipevar, teseluk, fotesen, tanesil.
You have 4 tests. Make your first move.

No single test settles everything here. There are 15 possible pairs and 2 possible rules, which makes 30 cases. Four yes/no tests can only tell apart 16 cases, so I'll pick each test to split the remaining cases as evenly as I can.

For the first test I'll put on three objects: nedupon, letesi and vipevar.
- **If one nexiom is enough:** the machine lights unless both nexioms are among the other three. That is 12 of the 15 pairs.
- **If both nexioms are needed:** it lights only if both are among these three. That is 3 of the 15 pairs.

So 15 of the 30 cases light up, which is an even split.

TEST: nedupon, letesi, vipevar
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

The machine did not light up. That leaves 15 possible cases:
- **If one nexiom is enough:** both nexioms must be among teseluk, fotesen and tanesil. That is 3 possible pairs.
- **If both are needed:** any pair works except one made only from nedupon, letesi and vipevar. That is 12 possible pairs.

Three yes/no tests can tell apart at most 8 cases, so I can't guarantee certainty. The best plan is to keep splitting the cases as evenly as possible.

Next I'll put on teseluk, fotesen, nedupon and letesi.
- **It lights up in 8 cases:**
  - One nexiom is enough and the pair is any two of teseluk, fotesen and tanesil (3 pairs).
  - Both are needed and the pair is teseluk–fotesen, teseluk–nedupon, teseluk–letesi, fotesen–nedupon or fotesen–letesi (5 pairs).
- **It stays dark in 7 cases:** both are needed and the pair is one of the 7 pairs with at least one of them off the machine.

TEST: teseluk, fotesen, nedupon, letesi
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

The machine stayed dark again. So "one nexiom is enough" is ruled out, because every pair that fit that rule would have lit up. The machine needs both nexioms.

That leaves 7 possible pairs:
- teseluk–vipevar
- teseluk–tanesil
- fotesen–vipevar
- fotesen–tanesil
- nedupon–tanesil
- letesi–tanesil
- vipevar–tanesil

Two yes/no tests can tell apart at most 4 cases, so I still can't be certain. I'll split the 7 pairs as evenly as I can.

Next I'll put on tanesil, nedupon, letesi and teseluk.
- **It lights up for 3 pairs:** nedupon–tanesil, letesi–tanesil and teseluk–tanesil.
- **It stays dark for 4 pairs:** teseluk–vipevar, fotesen–vipevar, fotesen–tanesil and vipevar–tanesil.

TEST: tanesil, nedupon, letesi, teseluk
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

The machine stayed dark again, so it still needs both nexioms. Any pair made only from tanesil, nedupon, letesi and teseluk is now ruled out.

That leaves 4 possible pairs:
- teseluk–vipevar
- fotesen–vipevar
- fotesen–tanesil
- vipevar–tanesil

One test can only split these into two groups, so the best I can do is narrow it to 2 pairs and then guess. I'll put on vipevar, teseluk and fotesen.
- **If it lights up:** the pair is teseluk–vipevar or fotesen–vipevar.
- **If it stays dark:** the pair is fotesen–tanesil or vipevar–tanesil.

TEST: vipevar, teseluk, fotesen
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

The last test stayed dark, so the machine still needs both nexioms. That rules out teseluk–vipevar and fotesen–vipevar, since all three of those objects were on the machine.

Two pairs fit every result:
- fotesen–tanesil
- vipevar–tanesil

None of my tests had fotesen and vipevar apart in a way that could tell these two pairs apart. So this is a 50/50 guess, and I'll pick fotesen–tanesil.

ANSWER: nexioms = fotesen, tanesil; needs = two

- **If both are needed:** it lights only if both nexioms are in the tested three. That is 3 pairs that light and 12 that stay dark.

Three tests give at most 8 outcomes, so I can't guarantee a correct answer. I'll keep splitting as evenly as possible.

Testing lidemo, fekara, bapanul and paralil:
- **Lights (8 cases):**
  - With the one-nexiom rule, all 3 remaining pairs include bapanul or paralil.
  - With the two-nexiom rule, the 5 pairs that light are L-Bp, L-P, F-Bp, F-P and Bp-P.
- **Stays dark (7 cases):** the two-nexiom rule is confirmed. The remaining pairs are every pair containing degakon, plus kurife-bapanul and kurife-paralil.

TEST: lidemo, fekara, bapanul, paralil
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

With the two-nexiom rule now confirmed, 7 pairs remain: lidemo-degakon, fekara-degakon, kurife-degakon, bapanul-degakon, paralil-degakon, kurife-bapanul and kurife-paralil. Two tests give at most 4 outcomes, so I'll split as evenly as I can.

Testing degakon, kurife and bapanul:
- **Lights (3 cases):** the pair is kurife-degakon, bapanul-degakon or kurife-bapanul.
- **Stays dark (4 cases):** the pair is lidemo-degakon, fekara-degakon, paralil-degakon or kurife-paralil.

One test has only two outcomes, so I can narrow this to 2 pairs but not to 1. My final answer will be a guess between those two.

Testing degakon, paralil and lidemo:
- **Lights:** the pair is lidemo-degakon or paralil-degakon.
- **Stays dark:** the pair is fekara-degakon or kurife-paralil.

TEST: degakon, paralil, lidemo

The last test leaves two possible pairs under the two-nexiom rule: fekara-degakon or kurife-paralil. No tests remain to tell them apart, so this answer is a guess with a 50% chance of being right. I'm choosing fekara-degakon.

- **Stays dark (7 left):** "needs two" pairs that include kupulos or zetolo.

Eight possibilities remain:

- **Needs two (5 pairs):** tadopes-kasiba, tadopes-sutugos, belutan-kasiba, belutan-sutugos, kasiba-sutugos.

- **Lights up:** all 3 "needs one" pairs, plus "needs two" with kasiba-sutugos.
- **Stays dark:** "needs two" with tadopes-kasiba, tadopes-sutugos, belutan-kasiba or belutan-sutugos.

Testing tadopes, kasiba and sutugos gives:

- **Stays dark:** belutan is a nexiom, so the pair is belutan-kasiba or belutan-sutugos.

The machine needs two nexioms, and tadopes is one of them. The other is either kasiba or sutugos, and no test is left to tell them apart. I'm guessing kasiba, which has a 50% chance of being right.
